reason: The text describes the Jewish people facing an external existential threat from Haman's decree to destroy them, and their mobilization in self-defense and celebration of deliverance. The narrative focuses on Mordecai and Esther's actions to save their people and the reversal of the evil decree. There is no depiction of the Hebrew/Jewish people complaining about their own leaders. Rather, Mordecai is portrayed positively as one who seeks the welfare of his people (דֹּרֵ֥שׁ טוֹב֙ לְעַמּ֔וֹ - 'seeking good for his people').
